{{reconstructed}}
==Proto-Semitic==

===Etymology===
Reconstructed in Militarev & Kogan's ''Semitic Etymological Dictionary'' as {{m|sem-pro||*ḫV(n)zīr-}}. The nasal is found in Arabic {{m|ar|خِنْزِير}} (whence the Modern South Arabian forms) and in Ge'ez {{m|gez|ኀንዚር|tr=ḫänzir}}, which the SED, after Zimmern and Leslau, takes to be an Aramaism; it rejects that explanation for Arabic, since no Aramaic form has the {{m|sem-pro||*-n-}}. Hebrew {{m|hbo|חֲזִיר}} probably continues an earlier {{m|sem-pro||*ḫuzīr-}} (Dead Sea Scrolls {{m|hbo|חוזיר|tr=ḥwzyr}}). Ugaritic alphabetic {{m|uga|𐎃𐎐𐎇𐎗}} and {{m|uga|𐎃𐎇𐎗}}, often compared, name a profession, not an animal; only the syllabic ''ḫu-zi-rù'' means “pig”. Akkadian {{m|akk|ḫuzīrum}} is reliably attested only in Old Assyrian and may have been the Assyrian word for the animal; the usual Akkadian term is {{m|akk|šaḫûm}}.
